subject: Priv infra IaC: ownership matrix, network boundaries, and CI handoff
messages:
From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@oakridge.example.com>
To: ava_chen@redwood.com
Cc: dev_patel@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-08-01T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Priv infra IaC — ownership + network questions

Hi Ava,

Thanks again for walking us through the private deployment overview yesterday. As we start mapping your Terraform/Helm modules into our change control, we ran into a couple of questions we hoped you and Dev could help clarify before our security review next week: 

1) Ownership: the spreadsheet you shared has a flat list of modules but no explicit runtime ownership (who takes pager/ops ownership after handoff). Can we get a concise owner matrix (team + primary contact + SLA) for each module?

2) Network boundaries: we need a clear diagram that calls out traffic flows between customer VPC, bastion, load balancers, and any encryption/MTU considerations for our on-prem SR-IOV NICs. We saw references to egress policies in the Helm values but not a top-level diagram.

3) CI/CD gating: our compliance team requires a short checklist of pipeline gates (e.g., tfsec, terratest integration, image provenance, signed Helm charts) and a recommended rollback window for the initial rollouts.

If you can attach an owner matrix CSV and a high-level network diagram, I can pass it to our InfoSec folks. We have a preliminary change window on Aug 10 but are flexible if you need more time.

Thanks,
Marta Lopez
Senior Cloud Ops
Oak Ridge Labs
[attachment: priv-iac-questions.txt (text/plain)]

From: ava_chen@redwood.com
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@oakridge.example.com>
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-01T11:07:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra IaC — ownership + network questions

Marta,

Appreciate the clear list. Attaching an initial draft of the ownership matrix and a network boundary diagram (see attachments). Quick notes inline below; Dev and Kim will add module-level CI details.

- Ownership matrix: columns are module, owning team (runtime/infra/security), primary contact, pager rota (Y/N), and recommended SLA target. We marked Redwood infra runtime as "Redwood Infra" for runtime-critical modules (gateway, kv-cache, scheduler). For customer-facing ingress modules we recommend "Customer NetOps" ownership post-handoff but Redwood covers the first 30-day stabilization window.

- Network diagram: high-level only — shows customer VPC, private subnet for inference nodes, NAT/bastion, and optional direct-connect to on-prem. We called out SR-IOV (MTU 9000) as an optional path; if you enable SR-IOV we recommend bumping the pod MTU and testing KV cache fragmentation.

Next steps: Dev will sketch the CI gate checklist and Rishi will propose a rollback cadence.

Regards,
Ava Chen
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
[attachment: priv-iac-ownership-matrix.csv (text/csv)] [attachment: network-boundaries-diagram.png (image/png)]

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@oakridge.example.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T08:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra IaC — ownership + network questions

Adding the CI/CD perspective — summary below and attached checklist. High-level gates we enforce in Dedicated/Private pipelines: 

- Static checks: tfsec + checkov with config baselines (fail on open security groups, non-encrypted state backend, hard-coded credentials).
- Unit/integration: terratest for critical TF modules (vpc, subnets, node pools). We run short, isolated tests in ephemeral sandbox accounts.
- Image provenance: enforce signed container images and SBOM metadata in Helm values (we generate attestations during build).
- Helm chart signing: ChartMuseum + cosign verification step in deploy pipeline.
- Canary and automatic rollback: our standard pattern is a 15-minute canary with traffic shifting (10% -> 50% -> 100%) and an automatic rollback if error-rate or latency regressions cross thresholds. For customers constrained by change windows we can shorten or extend the canary and provide a 72-hour escalation window.

Attached: ci-pipeline-checklist.md (short checklist you can give to your compliance team).

- Dev
[attachment: ci-pipeline-checklist.md (text/markdown)]

From: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@oakridge.example.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-02T13:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra IaC — ownership + network questions

Thanks — this is helpful. A couple of clarifying items from the compliance review:

- The matrix needs an explicit "post-handoff oncall owner" field for any module that touches customer data (we flagged kv-cache and audit-log-forwarder).
- Can you confirm whether the terraform state backend in Private is encrypted with a customer KMS or Redwood-managed KMS? The security team wants customer-managed KMS for regulated data.
- For the canary plan: we require an explicit traffic fallback plan if direct-connect latency spikes; can you add a short note on expected latency tolerances and whether the routing can failover to internet-egress?

If you can update the CSV and ci checklist with those two bullets we can greenlight the Aug 10 window.

— Marta

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marta Lopez <marta.lopez@oakridge.example.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-08-03T16:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Priv infra IaC — ownership + network questions

Marta — quick answers and updates attached. Summary: 

1) Post-handoff oncall owner: updated CSV now lists primary and secondary oncall (team email + rotation URL). For kv-cache and audit-forwarder the primary owner is Redwood Runtime Ops (runtime-oncall@redwood.com) and secondary is Customer NetOps (ops@oakridge.example.com) during the first 30 days.

2) Terraform state backend: for Private deployments we support both modes. We default to customer-managed KMS + customer S3/GCS bucket for regulated accounts. The module parameter is "state_backend.mode" (values: customer_managed | redwood_managed). The default for your account is set to customer_managed per contract - I attached the module snippet.

3) Canary fallback plan: added a one-paragraph fallback to the checklist — expected tolerances: direct-connect latency <= 20ms for KV operations, failover to internet-egress (TLS + mutual auth) is supported and will be triggered by routing policy if latency > 120ms or packet loss > 2% sustained for 2 minutes. We also added a manual rollback playbook for the Aug 10 change window.

Uploading final attachments: priv-iac-ownership-matrix.csv (v2), ci-pipeline-checklist.md (v2), network-boundaries-diagram.png (annotated). Let me know if you need us to open a SOC evidence request ticket; otherwise we can lock in Aug 10 with a 0800-1200 maintenance window.

Rishi Malhotra
Director, Runtime Reliability
Redwood Inference
[attachment: priv-iac-ownership-matrix-v2.csv (text/csv)] [attachment: ci-pipeline-checklist-v2.md (text/markdown)] [attachment: network-boundaries-diagram-annotated.png (image/png)]
